titre: Accélérer une recherche et lire son plan
note: La voix anglaise de « Accélérer une recherche et lire son plan » (module 1 : 14 novembre ; module 2 : 15 novembre) : chaque fichier garde l’id du français ; phrases : les légendes anglaises dites à voix haute ; cles : la légende française de chaque phrase (vkey).

elements.texte:
[cheerful] New lesson: speeding up a search and reading its plan.

Find out how to speed up searches and analyze how a query is run.
elements.apres: Since the start of module 8, you’ve been building the database for NutriBoost’s wellness workshops.
phrases: New lesson: speeding up a search and reading its plan.
Find out how to speed up searches and analyze how a query is run.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Since the start of module 8, you’ve been building the database for NutriBoost’s wellness workshops.

In the previous lesson, a view showed the box selection to the agency.

In the logistics department, the team scans each order’s QR code.

The screen should then show the products to prepare and their quantities.

But the screen shows “Looking up the order…”.

And the line of orders to prepare gets longer.
elements.avant: Find out how to speed up searches and analyze how a query is run.
elements.apres: With each scan, the app runs this query.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] With each scan, the app runs this query.

It looks for the order whose number is NB-10482.

The orders table holds 500,000 rows.

It also keeps the store’s old orders.

Your turn!

To check, you ask the database for its plan.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN, placed before the query, shows its plan.

Click the “Run” button.

EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows how the database plans to run the query.

Here, it goes through the table to find the order.

SCAN orders: all 500,000 rows are read, one by one.

Even the orders from 2019 are read again with each scan.

Your turn!

The bigger the table gets, the slower the search.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Your turn!

Your mission: create an index on the order number.

CREATE INDEX creates an index, here named idx underscore orders underscore number.

On orders, column order underscore number, sets the table and the column.

An index lets you find rows faster based on a value you’re looking for.

Here, the order number is used to find it.

Click the “Create the index” button.

The index sorts the numbers in order, each with its row’s identifier.

[cheerful] Run EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN again: click “Run”.

The database now uses the index to find the order.

Your turn!

SEARCH: thanks to the index, only the row you’re looking for is read.

The QR code of order NB-10482 is scanned again.

Léa Simon’s order is found right away.

And the line of orders moves again.
